articles.title: Pokémon Unite turns monster battles into a team sport
articles.summary: Pokémon Unite on the Nintendo Switch mashes up Pokémon with MOBAs like League of Legends and Dota 2, and a mobile version is launching in September.
articles.body: Games like League of Legends and Dota 2 are massively popular, and have been for the better part of a decade. But they can also be impenetrable to new players and viewers: there are so many characters and strategies that figuring out what’s happening on-screen is a huge challenge. The just-launched Pokémon Unite aims to fix that. It doesn’t just add cute monsters to the genre, but also some clever fixes to streamline it and make things more approachable. It’s kind of like a mashup of a strategy game and basketball, but with a Gengar thrown in. For the uninitiated, a MOBA — or multiplayer online battle arena, to use the genre’s unnecessarily long full name — is a five-on-five competition where the goal, usually, is to destroy the opposing team’s base. You do this by forming a squad of characters, each with their own unique abilities, which you use to steadily destroy towers and level up so you can push your way into your opponent’s territory. It’s often slow and methodical, a genre that rewards smart decisions as well as quick reflexes. Unite has many of these elements, including a varied cast of monsters to choose from. Charmander is a good all-around melee fighter, for instance, while Venasaur is better for ranged attacks. There are support characters and ones designed for defense. In a nice twist, many of the creatures will evolve over the course of the match. It’s fun starting out as a squat little Gible and ending the match as an imposing Garchomp. [Media: But the most interesting aspects of Unite are where it differs from the traditional MOBA. For starters, instead of trying to destroy your opponents’ base, you’re scoring points. To do this, you have to defeat wild pokémon that spawn throughout the arena to earn points, which you then take to one of the opponent’s goal circles to score. Drop enough points to destroy a circle and you can move on to the next. It’s similar to how MOBAs usually work, but it’s also a lot simpler to understand. And the system also adds some new drama: if you’re killed, you’ll lose a big chunk of the points you’re holding, which makes things very tense if you have a lot stacked up. The other nice thing about the game is that it has a strict time limit. Whereas a League of Legends match can stretch to close to an hour if it’s tightly contested, a single Pokémon Unite match takes exactly 10 minutes. Once the timer runs down, whichever team has the most points wins. (Some matches can actually be shorter; I’ve already played a few where the other team forfeited early because of a lopsided score.) The time limit and points system make Unite feel a bit more like a virtual sport, albeit one with experience points and spawning monsters. This idea of streamlining a MOBA isn’t exactly new. Blizzard tried it with Heroes of the Storm, and Riot did something similar when it brought League of Legends to mobile with the spinoff Wild Rift. But, at least from what I’ve played so far, Unite seems the most approachable. The rules are easy to understand, the matches are short and intense, and the world is already something millions of people know and love. So far, the only real issue I’ve run into is the copious amounts of virtual currency you can earn or buy. It gets weirdly complicated, to the point that you can spend as much time messing around in battle pass menus as actually playing the game. It doesn’t seem like you have to buy anything, but some of the fashion options are pretty tempting. Right now, Pokémon Unite is available as a free download on the Nintendo Switch, but it’s poised to become even bigger when it debuts on mobile in September (with crossplay and cross progression at launch). Developer TiMi, an internal studio at Tencent, already operates two of the biggest games in the world with Call of Duty: Mobile and Honor of Kings. The combination of Pokémon and MOBA could soon add a third.

articles.title: 'Shooters fired at actor Tiger Shroff on 3rd attempt, did recce of other actors including Salman, Aamir': Mumbai Police
articles.summary: Mumbai police say Oct 18 shooters made a third attempt on Tiger Shroff after recce of Salman Khan, Aamir Khan, Akshay Kumar and Amitabh Bachchan; two injured.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The October 18 firing at actor Tiger Shroff was allegedly the third attempt by the shooters to target him, with the accused claiming during interrogation that they had conducted reconnaissance of several Bollywood actors before zeroing in on Shroff, police sources said.According to sources, the three shooters, Phool Singh, 19, Rehan Ansari, 19, and Rithik Mahato, 22, told investigators that in the first week of October, they allegedly received instructions from Lawrence Bishnoi gangster Anil Pandit to identify potential targets, including actors Salman Khan, Aamir Khan, Akshay Kumar and Amitabh Bachchan.The accused allegedly recced these actors but failed to locate them or found it difficult to get close to them. Pandit subsequently, through voice notes, instructed them to target Tiger Shroff, son of actor Jackie Shroff.During the second week of October, the accused allegedly learnt that Tiger regularly worked out at MMV Matrix Gym, owned by his family, on Linking Road in Khar.The shooters reportedly spotted the actor outside the gym on one occasion but were not prepared to carry out the attack.“They decided to return the next day at the same time, but Tiger did not turn up. They then asked an auto-rickshaw driver where they could get to see filmstars. The driver allegedly told them that they could spot Tiger Shroff at a ground near Pushpa Park in Juhu where he regularly comes to play football,” a source said.Acting on this information, the shooters allegedly lay in wait at the ground on October 11, but Tiger did not arrive. They subsequently returned on October 18, allegedly armed and prepared to execute the attack.The firing left Tiger’s driver and a vlogger injured, while the actor escaped with minor injuries. articles.title: Kristen Bell locked doors ‘from the outside’ to keep Dax Shepard from confronting boy who ignored their daughter
articles.summary: “I was like, ‘Are you kidding me, my friend?’” the podcaster thought when seeing the kid. “This is the number one girl in America.”
articles.body:
Kristen Bell had to go to extreme lengths to keep Dax Shepard from confronting a boy around their daughter's age.

The Frozen star says she had to "lock the doors from the outside with the key just to make sure Dax didn't knock on the little boy's door that evening."

Shepard's fury came in response to the boy ignoring their daughter after she presented him with a valentine.

Dax Shepard is a protective dad — which means Kristen Bell needs to be a protective wife.

The actors, who have been married for 13 years and share two children, appeared together on Monday's episode of Shepard's Armchair Expert podcast. Bell was joined by her Nobody Wants This costars Adam Brody, Justine Lupe, and Timothy Simons to discuss the hit Netflix show when the conversation turned to the perils of Valentine's Day pageantry.

"We had a valentine mishap this year, and it was the hardest. It's the most pain I've been in in a decade," Shepard managed to share, discomfort visible on his face. "We had a little one who'd had a Valentine, and then that Valentine didn't really acknowledge her all day, and she had done so much. I was like, 'I'm gonna f---ing kill this prick,'" Shepard laughed.

Bell then noted, "I had to lock the doors from the outside with the key just to make sure Dax didn't knock little boy's door that evening."

Shepard reasoned out loud, "I was like, 'Are you kidding me, my friend? Do you know what you got here on the hook? This is the number one girl in America.'" But ultimately, he explained how he saw both sides of the situation. "I realized [the] next time I was in class and I was eyeing up this little f---er, I was like, 'Oh yeah, boys don't know what the hell is going on.'"

Bell concurred: "He completely forgot that it was that day."

Monica Padman, Shepard's cohost, added that the debacle proved to her how much this particular daughter of Shepard's and Bell's "is so your daughter," explaining, "A week later I was like, 'I'm really sorry that happened.' She was like, 'Oh, it's fine. He didn't mean it.' She immediately had an understanding that it wasn't personal. I was like, 'How are you 11 and can do that?'"

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

Shepard and Bell share two girls — Lincoln, born in 2013, and Delta, born in 2014. Though the family of four are the picture of a happy Hollywood family, the Veronica Mars actress has been candid about the struggles she's faced as a working mom .

"It's hard. Do not think because I am on your television that it is easy for me," she admitted in an interview last week. "It's brutal. I cry weekly." She then shared some of the questions she frequently asks herself when considering jobs: "Is this going to pull me away from my kids too much? Will I still be able to be the mom that I want to be? That's really the number one, to be honest. There's nothing higher than that... I would easily let my whole career and all its legacy and notoriety 'disapparate' tomorrow if it meant sacrificing something major in my kids' lives, or not being there."

articles.title: Executivo que apostou em Paralamas do Sucesso e Legião Urbana expõe em livro o equilíbrio delicado entre arte e comércio que rege a indústria do disco | G1
articles.standfirst: Os fatos legitimam as proezas contadas por Jorge Davidson em autobiografia que descortina bastidores das carreiras de nomes como Adriana Calcanhotto, Fernanda Abreu, Gabriel O Pensador e Skank.
articles.summary: Os fatos legitimam as proezas contadas por Jorge Davidson em autobiografia que descortina bastidores das carreiras de nomes como Adriana Calcanhotto, Fernanda Abreu, Gabriel O Pensador e Skank.
articles.body:
Jorge Davidson posa com Herbert Vianna, vocalista e guitarrista dos Paralamas do Sucesso, banda que indicou para a gravadora EMI em 1983 — Foto: Arquivo pessoal Jorge Davidson

Título: “Em sintonia com o sucesso – A arte de revelar talentos na música brasileira”

♬ Em fevereiro de 1993, quando Jorge Davidson assumiu a diretoria artística da gravadora Sony Music, vindo de experiência bem-sucedida na EMI, período em que abriu as portas da companhia para bandas então iniciantes como Blitz, Paralamas do Sucesso e Legião Urbana , o executivo encontrou o nome do grupo Cidade Negra na lista de cortes da Sony. Após um primeiro álbum bem-sucedido, “Lute pra viver” (1990), a banda fluminense de reggae viu o sucesso escapulir com o segundo disco, “Negro no poder” (1992), e ia ser impiedosamente limada do elenco da gravadora.

Fã de reggae e confiante no talento do grupo, Davidson negociou a permanência do Cidade Negra na Sony Music e remodelou o som e o repertório da banda, após driblar a resistência inicial do guitarrista Da Ghama, dando polimento pop no reggae do Cidade Negra.

Com a decisão do vocalista Rás Bernardo de sair do grupo, Toni Garrido foi escolhido para ser o cantor do Cidade Negra, Liminha foi convidado para produzir o terceiro álbum da banda e Davidson foi atrás de repertório, conseguindo a canção “Onde você mora?”, parceria de Marisa Monte com Nando Reis. A empreitada deu certo e o terceiro álbum do grupo, “Sobre todas as forças”, se tornou um discos blockbusters de 1994.

A virada do Cidade Negra é uma das muitas histórias saborosas contadas por Jorge Davidson ao longo das 380 páginas de “Em sintonia com o sucesso – A arte de revelar talentos na música brasileiro”, livro de memórias musicais deste baiano de criação carioca que atuou como radialista antes de se tornar um dos executivos mais importantes da indústria fonográfica brasileira, com atuação decisiva na maior parte do tempo – cerca de 30 anos – em que trabalhou no mercado de disco, geralmente no cargo de diretor artístico.

Lançamento da editora Gryphus, o livro engrena quando, após narrar histórias pessoais da vida saboreada entre a praia e os campos de futebol, Davidson entra na área profissional. A rigor, “Em sintonia com o sucesso – A arte de revelar talentos na música brasileiro” é um livro sobre o equilíbrio delicado entre arte e comércio. E, justiça seja feita, os fatos legitimam as proezas contadas por Davidson na autobiografia.

Quando ainda atuava no departamento internacional da EMI, gravadora na qual ingressou na indústria fonográfica, vindo do rádio, Davidson fez algumas jogadas decisivas, atuando como um meio-de-campo que indicou à direção artística da gravadora as bandas Blitz e Paralamas do Sucesso, ambas contratadas por conta destes dois movimentos do antenado Davidson. Tanto que logo o chefão da multinacional o indicou para ser o diretor artístico da EMI, decisão que desagradou Miguel Plopschi e Renato Côrrea, então dividindo o cargo.

Uma vez efetivado como diretor artístico da EMI, Davidson marcou logo um golaço com a contratação da banda Legião Urbana, decisão tomada instantaneamente após ouvir uma fita cassete com o suprassumo do cancioneiro de Renato Russo (1960 – 1996) na fase inicial da Legião. A fita tinha sido entregue ao executivo por Pedro Ribeiro – irmão do baixista dos Paralamas do Sucesso, Bi Ribeiro – e surtiu efeito imediato em Davidson. O diretor artístico detectou ali a genialidade de Renato Russo. E o resto foi (mais) uma história que Davidson conta com orgulho no livro.

Sem jamais maquiar as disputas de poder em uma gravadora, Davidson concentra a narrativa nos próprios feitos, figurando na história como um herói sempre a salvar os artistas de eventuais incompreensões de presidentes e funcionários dos departamentos de marketing. Foi assim quando ficou ao lado de Fernanda Abreu, contra todos na EMI, e defendeu a capa conceitual idealizada pela artista para o primeiro álbum solo da cantora revelada na Blitz, “Sla radical dance disco club”, editado em 1990.

Ao longo do livro, fica evidente como as ótimas relações de Jorge Davidson com nomes poderosos na indústria da música – casos de Mariozinho Rocha (diretor musical da TV Globo de 1989 a 2016, período em que Mariozinho decidia boa parte das músicas que entrariam nas trilhas sonoras das novelas) e de Antônio Augusto Amaral de Carvalho Filho, Tutinha, chefão da rádio Jovem Pan, emissora paulistana decisiva na promoção de uma música – também foram fundamentais para que as apostas artísticas do executivo dessem frutos comerciais.

Foi a Tutinha que Davidson apresentou, por exemplo, as músicas do primeiro álbum de Gabriel O Pensador antes do lançamento do disco em 1993. O aval do radialista foi fundamental para o sucesso do álbum, pontuado por hits radiofônicos como “Lôraburra”. Só que o rapper não bisou o sucesso inicial ao lançar o segundo disco, “Ainda é só o começo” (1995), e levou um puxão de orelhas de Davidson ao apresentar ao diretor artístico o repertório do terceiro álbum.

Como o próprio Pensador conta no texto que escreveu para a orelha do livro, ouviu de Davidson que o repertório estava aquém do potencial criativo do rapper. Resultado: o artista foi para a casa e compôs músicas como “2345meia78” e “Cachimbo da paz ”, ambas decisivas para que o álbum “Quebra-cabeça” se tornasse um dos discos mais bem-sucedidos de 1997, superando o milhão de cópias vendidas.

Se Jorge Davidson contribuiu para o fortalecimento do pop rock brasileiro na primeira das duas vezes em que trabalhou para a gravadora EMI, apostando em bandas consagradas e eternizadas pelo público, o período na Sony Music foi essencial para o desenvolvimento das discografias de Jota Quest, Skank e Chico Science & Nação Zumbi, bandas também fundamentais, todas contratadas sob a direção artística de Davidson.

Sem falar na contribuição para a consolidação da carreira de Adriana Calcanhotto, artista que, segundo Davidson, era incompreendida na Sony quando o executivo assumiu a direção artística da companhia em 1993. De fato, foi com a entrada da canção “Mentiras” (1992) na trilha sonora da novela “Renascer” (TV Globo, 1993) que a carreira de Calcanhotto deslanchou, com a cantora já empresariada por Mauro Benzaquem, indicação de Davidson.

As contextualizações, datas e dados salpicados ao longo do livro valorizam a narrativa porque estão sempre corretos, com exceção da afirmação, na página 218, de que os CDs dominaram o mercado em 1987 quando, no Brasil, as bolachinhas prateadas somente se tornaram hegemônicas na indústria fonográfica a partir da primeira metade da década de 1990 (no mundo, os CDs superaram os LPs em vendas somente em 1989). Detalhe que não tira o mérito de um livro que interessará a todo mundo que gosta de saber como a música é produzida antes de chegar ao consumidor.

Jorge Davidson deu contribuição fundamental ao universo pop brasileiro quando foi diretor artístico da EMI e da Sony Music. Na BMG, gravadora para qual migrou em 1997, a convite do presidente Luiz Oscar Niemeyer, a contribuição do executivo foi menos relevante do ponto de vista artístico.

Ainda assim, merecem menções honrosas as contratações de Lenine – cuja carreira solo foi enfim iniciada naquele ano de 1997 com o álbum “O dia em que faremos contato”, lançado sob a égide de Davidson – e de Ana Carolina, além da transformação do Pato Fu em uma banda de sucesso. Em área popular, foi Davidson quem orquestrou a contratação e lançamento de Wanessa Camargo em 2000 como cantora de pop adolescente.

Enfim, é inegável que Jorge Davidson domina a arte de revelar e/ou lapidar talentos na música brasileira. O livro de memórias deste baiano de alma carioca presta ótimo serviço à bibliografia musical brasileira ao revelar que o sucesso é fruto sobretudo do talento artístico, mas também da habilidade para promover um disco no mercado. Sem essa habilidade, um grande talento pode nunca chegar aos ouvidos do público.

Em essência, o livro mostra que conduzir um artista pelo caminho do sucesso foi a arte exercida por Jorge Davidson com faro e sensibilidade ao longo de três décadas de atuação decisiva na indústria do disco.

articles.title: De Pussycat Dolls a Gusttavo Lima: 5 histórias que explicam publicidade em letras de música | G1
articles.standfirst: Do e-mail vazado sobre o grupo pop americano aos cachês milionários para falar de bebida alcoólica no sertanejo, entenda como mercado testou transformar refrãos em vitrines.
articles.summary: Do e-mail vazado sobre o grupo pop americano aos cachês milionários para falar de bebida alcoólica no sertanejo, entenda como mercado testou transformar refrãos em vitrines.
articles.body:
O anúncio da primeira vinda das Pussycat Dolls ao Brasil, com show em São Paulo no dia 30 de outubro , é um bom motivo para relembrar uma movimentação curiosa nos bastidores da indústria musical.

A ideia de vender espaço publicitário dentro de versos e refrãos já pareceu ser parte de um futuro inescapável, mas o mercado precisou testar o formato na prática para entender o que realmente funcionava. E essa história tem a ver com nomes que vão das Pussycat até Gusttavo Lima.

Relembre cinco momentos que explicam esta tendência:

Em 2008, mensagens de um empresário chamado Adam Kluger caíram nas caixas de entrada de vários jornalistas por acidente. O objetivo dele era claro: vender espaço publicitário nas letras das Pussycat Dolls. Na época, liguei para o número de telefone que estava no rodapé do e-mail. O cara foi um pouco ríspido, mas resumiu bem o seu modelo de negócio:

"A gente tem as celebridades e eles têm o dinheiro".

Na mesma ligação, no entanto, ele garantiu que nenhuma música das Pussycat Dolls acabou sendo vendida.

Se as Pussycat Dolls passaram ilesas, outros artistas da Kluger Agency abraçaram a ideia. O rapper Flo Rida foi quem efetivamente comercializou seus versos. A música “Hey Jasmin” falava sobre a Live Jasmin, uma plataforma de webcam com modelos que funcionava como uma espécie de OnlyFans da época. Depois, ele lançou “Zoosk Girl”, dedicada ao aplicativo de namoro Zoosk, um precursor do Tinder.

A capa do álbum 'Doll Domination', lançado pelas Pussycat Dolls em 2008 — Foto: Divulgação

Essas iniciativas no fim dos anos 2000 criaram a expectativa de que a inserção paga de marcas nas canções seria massificada. Para os críticos, era o ápice da mercantilização musical. No fim, a experiência não decolou lá fora. A indústria concluiu que usar produtos de forma visual nos videoclipes funcionava muito bem, mas transformar o refrão em uma vitrine sonora pegava mal com os fãs.

Se a tática soou forçada para o pop estrangeiro, no Brasil, o mercado sertanejo encontrou nela uma fórmula de alto lucro. Gusttavo Lima faturou pelo menos R$ 1 milhão para citar o uísque Old Parr no sucesso “Zé da Recaída”, lançado em 2018. Dois anos depois, a dupla Zé Neto & Cristiano escancarou o formato com "Alô Ambev", uma faixa que transita exatamente no limite entre uma balada de sofrência e um jingle da Brahma.

5) A coca-cola gelada (e não remunerada)

Hoje, a venda de espaços diretos nas composições é algo raro. O mais comum segue sendo quando um artista cita uma marca sem ganhar cachê, apenas pela fluidez da narrativa. É o que acontece quando ouvimos nomes como Caetano Veloso e Lulu Santos cantando sobre política, juventude ou amor enquanto citam uma coca-cola gelada. Tudo orgânico e sem patrocínio. No fim das contas, o que vingou mesmo foram as parcerias visuais em clipes, cotas de turnês e redes sociais: todos querem as marcas por perto, mas quase ninguém quer abrir mão da própria letra.

articles.title: Jack Antonoff slams Ed Sheeran over Macklemore controversy, says he should have canceled tour: ‘Stand the f--- up’
articles.summary: The Bleachers frontman also stated that saying “Free Palestine” is “not in any way a strange, uncomfortable or controversial thing to say, it’s a deeply huma...
articles.body:
Jack Antonoff criticized Ed Sheeran for proceeding with his tour after Macklemore's removal.

The Bleachers frontman said that Sheeran should have opted to "cancel the whole f---ing tour, then play for free outside each venue" to "raise a bunch of money."

Antonoff told Sheeran to "stand the f--- up" and opined that saying "Free Palestine" is "not in any way a strange, uncomfortable or controversial thing."

Jack Antonoff doesn't think Ed Sheeran handled his recent controversy well.

The Bleachers frontman criticized the "Shape of You" singer for proceeding with his Loop tour after Macklemore was removed from the lineup due to objections to his pro-Palestine comments on stage.

Though he has expressed solidarity with Palestine for years, Antonoff said that he has "felt way more emboldened to say" "Free Palestine" in public and on stage since the Macklemore debacle. "It's not in any way a strange, uncomfortable or controversial thing to say, it's a deeply human thing to say," he told The Guardian . "If you think it is [controversial] you're lost in some other sauce that is so crazy."

Antonoff condemned Sheeran, who blamed Macklemore's removal from the tour on a promoter who objected to the rapper's comments.

"They're going to let some f---ing promoter tell me what I can say? Don't book me. I'll play for free outside," he said. "[Ed Sheeran] missed a massive, beautiful opportunity there: just cancel the whole f---ing tour, then play for free outside each venue, raise a bunch of money, rather than let a f---ing billionaire tell you what to do."

He added, "The reason it's not an anomaly or niche issue is because we all live in a world where billionaires are constantly telling us what to do. So stand the f--- up."

Entertainment Weekly has reached out to representatives for Sheeran for comment.

Macklemore made comments advocating for Palestinian liberation and criticizing Israel on stage during his opening set of Sheeran's show in New Jersey on Sept. 5. A week later, Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of the Loop tour, told Rolling Stone that "We have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup," prompting Macklemore's removal.

"To all of my Jewish brothers and sisters, criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide, it in no way is criticism of you," Macklemore said during the show. "This message is for peace, love, for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect, and equality."

Shortly after Macklemore's exit, all of the remaining musicians attached to the tour dropped out in solidarity, including opening acts Finneas, Aaron Rowe, and Lukas Graham, as well as Sheeran's backing band Beoga.

Sheeran released a statement refusing to take a side in the Israel-Palestine conflict, and wept on stage during his first concert after Macklemore's removal as he said, "I've had to take and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I'm so sorry."

Macklemore launched a three-concert "Free Palestine" tour in Europe, with all proceeds going toward organizations supporting Palestinian people.

articles.title: Neil Young Sues Trump Committee for $10 Million Over Use of ‘Rockin’ in the Free World’
articles.summary: The fundraising committee played the anthem at a rally this month despite a prior settlement barring such use without permission from Young himself, the laws...
articles.body:
Rock legend Neil Young has slapped a Trump fundraising committee with a $10 million lawsuit over the use of his song, "Rockin' in the Free World," at an Ohio rally this month.

According to the five-page filing obtained by Rolling Stone , Trump was "personally aware that a license would be required" to play the song at an event, and he also knew Young "has not and would not grant the required license." The unauthorized use happened despite a prior lawsuit and 2020 settlement in which Trump allegedly agreed never to use Young's music without permission, the new complaint states. (Trump is not named as an individual defendant in the Monday complaint.)

"'Rockin' in the Free World' is a blistering anthem that contrasts the hollow promises of American political rhetoric with the harsh realities faced by the poor, homeless, and forgotten," Young and his lawyers, Robert Besser and Scott Simmons, wrote in the new complaint. "The lyrics paint vivid street-level portraits of a mother discarding her baby, addicts lost in despair, garbage piling in the shadows of prosperity, while the repeated chorus delivers a savage irony, celebrating freedom that clearly isn't shared by all."

They added that the 1989 song, which was named Rolling Stone's best vintage rock song of 2026 , "is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for."

There was no immediate answer to a request for comment sent to the White House, the Trump 47 Committee, and the Republican National Committee, which partnered with Trump to create the joint fundraising committee.

Young's legal sparring with Trump dates back to 2015, when Trump used the track during his now infamous Trump Tower announcement that he was running for president. Young immediately condemned the move.

"Donald Trump was not authorized to use 'Rockin' in the Free World' in his presidential candidacy announcement," a Young spokesperson said in a statement then. "Neil Young, a Canadian citizen, is a supporter of Bernie Sanders for President of the United States of America."

When Trump played the song again in 2018, Young objected again. "I asked him then, in a widely shared, public letter to cease and desist," Young wrote on his website at the time. "However, he chose not to listen to my request, just as he chooses not to listen to the many American voices who ask him to stop his constant lies, to stop his petty, nasty name-calling, and bullying, to stop pushing his dangerous, vilifying and hateful rhetoric."

Young, 80, filed the latest lawsuit in federal court in Virginia, where the fundraising committee is based. He said the song was played on Oct. 12 at a rally in Youngstown, Ohio, where Trump made a speech.

Young is far from the only artist to challenge Trump over the use of music at his political events. The White Stripes, Rihanna , Axl Rose, Pharrell Williams , Linkin Park, and the estates of Tom Petty and Sinéad O'Connor have all publicly objected to his use of their songs.

articles.title: Jay-Z to headline Super Bowl halftime show
articles.summary: Jay-Z has helped select artists for the last several Super Bowl halftime shows.
articles.body: Jay-Z has helped select artists for the last several Super Bowl halftime shows. Now, the 25-time Grammy winner and mogul will step into the performer role as the headliner for the 2027 show. The NFL and Apple Music announced the news on social media during Monday night’s game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles, confirming recent reporting about the halftime show from Puck that cited industry sources. “GOAT’s out of the bag,” read the post, which featured a black-and-white video of Jay-Z in the stands with a goat on his lap as “Allow me to reintroduce myself,” the opening line of his song “Public Service Announcement (Interlude)” plays. Jay-Z’s entertainment company, Roc Nation, has been a partner with the NFL and produced the halftime show since 2019. “For several years, we’ve had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I’ve seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show,” NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. “When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.” Super Bowl 61 will take place Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, near Los Angeles. The game and the halftime show will air on ESPN, ABC and Disney+ and on mobile devices with NFL+. Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, just wrapped his 30 Tour, which celebrated the 30th anniversary of his debut album, “Reasonable Doubt.” His final two shows were at SoFi. “From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” he said in a statement Monday. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.” During the tour, which featured stops in Paris, London and Jay-Z’s hometown, New York City, he brought up several guests, including his wife, superstar Beyoncé. It’s unclear whether Bey or any of Jay-Z’s many other famous friends and collaborators will make cameos during the halftime performance. Many artists who have headlined the event have brought on major stars. But several, including The Weeknd and Rihanna, chose to shine solo when they appeared at the event. Last year’s game, which was broadcast on NBC and Peacock, featured Bad Bunny as the headliner, with Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin making cameos. The performance was awarded seven Creative Arts Emmys this year, making it the most awarded halftime show in history. It was Bad Bunny’s first Emmy and Jay-Z’s third, with both artists serving as producers last year. Kendrick Lamar, who headlined the 2025 show, also took home an Emmy after he tackled the gig. Next year, said Apple’s vice president of music and international content, Oliver Schusser, fans can expect “an incredible show” from Jay-Z, whose “impact on global music culture is as profound as it is undeniable.”

articles.summary: French actor and filmmaker Melanie Laurent, best known her work in Quentin Tarantino’s ‘Inglourious Basterds’, has joined Saif Ali Khan and Vidya Balan in
articles.body: French actor and filmmaker Melanie Laurent, best known her work in Quentin Tarantino’s ‘Inglourious Basterds’, has joined Saif Ali Khan and Vidya Balan in filmmaker Ritesh Batra’s upcoming feature film ‘Long Years Ago’.The comedy-drama that went into production in Mumbai, is reportedly set in 1991 and revolves around a family that has spent years avoiding difficult conversations. According to the official description, ‘Long Years Ago’ “is the story of a family that has gone too long without saying the things that matter, and what happens when they’re finally forced to find the words.”Speaking about the project, Batra expressed his excitement about bringing the cast together. “I am tremendously honored to be working with Saif, Vidya and Melanie, and to see these great actors bring characters that are so close to my heart to life,” the filmmaker said to Deadline.Laurent also spoke about her long-standing connection with the director, revealing that they had discussed the possibility of working together years ago. “I met Ritesh fifteen years ago at the Marrakech Film Festival, and we shared this dream to meet in Mumbai one day. I immediately loved this new project, and I am more than honoured and happy to be a part of it,” she said in a statement to Deadline.Vidya, on the other hand, shared her excitement to reunite with Saif, decades after starring together in 'Parineeta'. She said, "There’s such a beautiful sensitivity and honesty to his storytelling. What makes this even more special is that I get to reunite with Saif after Parineeta, my very first film! I can’t wait to experience the magic of working with both Ritesh and Saif."Leading man Saif, also shared his excitement about the film and present the audience with a 'deeply moving story'.Batra first gained international recognition with his 2013 feature ‘The Lunchbox’, starring Irrfan Khan and Nimrat Kaur. The film premiered at the Cannes Film Festival and went on to become one of the notable Indian releases of the year. He subsequently directed ‘Our Souls at Night’, starring Robert Redford and Jane Fonda, and ‘Photograph’, featuring Nawazuddin Siddiqui and Sanya Malhotra, which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival.Laurent, meanwhile, has built an international career as an actor and filmmaker. articles.title: Netizens respond to Rashmika Mandanna's post defending Vijay Deverakonda and their relationship: ‘Etna explanation to Vijay se expect kiya tha…’
articles.summary: Rashmika Mandanna shares a heartfelt statement defending her relationship with Vijay Deverakonda, addressing online criticism after their appearance on 'Koffee with Karan.' The couple receives both support and backlash from netizens. Read more about their journey and Mandanna's response to the ongoing debate.
articles.body: Rashmika Mandanna and Vijay Deverakonda's relationship has sparked a lot of interest online over the past couple of days. Following their first appearance as a couple on ‘Koffee with Karan,' many netizens criticised the actor for his comments. During the interview, he shared that he told Rashmika she had to ask him to marry her 100 times, while the actress revealed she spent an entire year convincing him before they agreed to tie the knot.Amid ongoing online criticism, Mandanna shared a lengthy statement about the matter, saying people do not need to worry about their relationship, as she is truly happy with Deverakonda. Netizens were quick to react to her post online, with many people sharing their support for the couple’s bond and relationship, while others still had their own qualms about the matter.Netizens react to Rashmika Mandanna’s post about her and Vijay Deverakonda's relationshipMany people flooded the actress’ comment section under the post with heart emojis, lending their support to the star and her relationship with Deverakonda. One person shared a comment and thanked the actress for her genuine words, while another person shared, “Every single word here is pure truth and so empowering! Thank you for speaking your heart out so gracefully, ma'am. Standing by each other through thick and thin is what true love is all about. We are always, always with you both!”One person wrote, “I appreciate this response... It seems she gets to live with a different version of him than the one coming across to us... Just have to trust she knows what is good for her instead of implying otherwise out of 'concern'," while another social media user added, “Such a lovely couple you guys are. Lots of love, Vijju and Rushiee.”Internet users also joked about Rashmika Mandanna’s lengthy post and called her outWhile there were many supporters, there were also comments from people who criticised the situation. One social media user joked about the ongoing debate in the comment section and wrote, “She proved once again 'how much she loves Vijay.' Vijay proved once again ‘how much he loves himself.’”Another similar comment on her post added, “If you can’t read all those pages of paragraphs, here’s a short summary for you: 'Rashmika loves Vijay, and Vijay loves Vijay too,'" while another person added, “Posting this was brave; leaving it open for comments was braver.” Another internet user resharing the post on his account and added a similar comment saying: “9 slides ki post daali hai inhone just to prove ‘Rashmika loves Vijay and Vijay loves Vijay too’”, further mentioning that Deverakonda simply shared a photo and the same video his partner has posted online, and barely wrote about the incident in the caption.Netizens call out Vijay Deverakonda for not sharing a post about the ongoing matterMany people online continued to call out the ‘Arjun Reddy’ actor, pointing out that while Mandanna took the initiative to share a lengthy post about the criticism online, he is still keeping quiet. One person wrote on Instagram, “No reply from him, typical," while another added, “Did he give a remark, birthmark, postmark, trademark, hallmark, watermark, or checkmark???”Another comment from a netizen added, “Brother is still asking his girl to answer all this s***. The problem wasn't taking time to answer the proposal, but the red flags were validated throughout the interview. The fact that he came across as too self-obsessed gave me jitters in a very bad way.” Another person called her and Deverakonda out and wrote, “Etna explanation to Vijay se expect kiya tha, not from you” (Such an explanation was expected from Vijay, not from you).Rasmika Mandanna’s statement about her and Vijay Deverakonda’s relationshipOn Monday, Mandanna officially shared a post on her account about the ongoing drama revolving around her relationship with Vijay Deverakonda. She started the post by commenting that she wanted to share her “lil’ 2 cents” on the matter.She continued, “I generally don't address these things because everyone has a right to their opinions. Sometimes, I even enjoy reading them and gaining a different perspective. But the current frenzy over our interview feels less like people having opinions and more like an angry mob looking for someone to vent at.”She provided clarification over the “100 times” comment that was made on "Koffee With Karan," writing that she was in shock over the ongoing hate and speculation about their relationship. She added, “First, it was never about the number of times or an entire year. That's where some of you got stuck. Yes, that conversation happened. But neither of us was looking for a grand proposal. The conversation was about him wanting both of us to take the time and space to understand each other, to be sure that despite all the highs and lows and the joys and stresses of life, this was what we wanted and the right time for it. And we did. We chose each other.”She also shared that neither of them was looking for a grand gesture and that she respected his decision to take a year to be more sure about things in life. She also commented on when it became a “bad thing” to be “obsessed” with your man. Mandanna also added, “Find a man who loves you so beautifully that even after you're married, you'd still want to tell him, ‘Let's get married.' I would do it a thousand times—100 is nothing. It's really that simple.”Lastly, she concluded the post by sharing a video of Deverakonda carrying her on his back, while she wrote in the post, “Love to all those who celebrate love and joy. And to everyone else ... Please find something that makes you happy, too.”Rashmika Mandanna and Vijay Deverakonda met for the first time in 2017 while working together on the set of their Telugu film ‘Geetha Govindam,' which was released in 2018. The pair started dating soon after they worked on their second film, ‘Dear Comrade,' together. They officially tied the knot on February 26, 2026, in Udaipur.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Chethan D’Souza reveals how Rajinikanth and Hrithik Roshan’s ‘Jailer 2’ scene was planned to give both stars equal attention; reveals Mohanlal performed driving stunt himself
articles.summary: Action director Chethan D’Souza has spoken about designing the action sequences for ‘Jailer 2’ and working with superstars Rajinikanth and Mohanlal.
articles.body: Action director Chethan D’Souza has spoken about designing the action sequences for ‘Jailer 2’ and working with superstars Rajinikanth and Mohanlal. He shared how the team planned the stunts while keeping the actors’ safety in mind and explained why Rajinikanth’s style and involvement make him special. He also discussed balancing Rajinikanth and Hrithik Roshan in a scene, explaining how the action choreography is planned to give both characters the right attention without one overshadowing the other.In a conversation with Variety India, the action director shared that action sequences involving big stars require careful planning. The team works on the emotions, build-ups and choreography well before filming begins.How Chethan D’Souza plans action for superstars“High-octane action in big-budget films, especially those featuring superstars, must be scripted and carefully planned. The emotions, build-ups and action need to flow together. We establish these moments in advance because the actors’ time and safety matter,” he said.He further added that creating a heroic moment is not always about how well an actor fights. A star’s style, swagger and screen presence also play an important role.“We consider how to bring the actor’s star appeal into the choreography. With stars, it is often less about how well they fight and more about their style and swagger. Safety remains central. We consider the actor’s age, capabilities and what looks convincing on screen, then design the action accordingly,” he said.Chethan revealed that Malayalam veteran Mohanlal performed a driving stunt himself under his direction, including driving at high speed. However, dangerous moments involving explosions and collisions with vehicles or aircraft require technology rather than being filmed live.Balancing Rajinikanth and Hrithik Roshan‘Jailer 2’ also features Hrithik Roshan in a special appearance with Rajinikanth. Chethan shared about balancing two major stars in the same scene begins with the script. The director explains the sequence, after which the action team develops the details and adds ideas to improve the scene.“That balance is established in the script, not improvised on set,” he said.He said the team plans everything, from a vehicle’s arrival and impact to the actor stepping out and the shots that follow. He said, “We work out details such as the vehicle’s arrival and impact, the actor stepping down, and the shots that follow to make the entrance iconic. Each character needs the right emphasis without overpowering or being overshadowed by the other. Hrithik’s character must work in harmony with Rajini sir’s. We plan this well before filming and assess whether it will work.”Chethan also shared about Rajinikanth’s involvement with the action sequences. He revealed that the Superstar approached the work with the enthusiasm of a newcomer.“He was completely involved and approached the work with the openness of a newcomer. I never felt, even for a day, that I was working with a superstar. He stays on set rather than retreat to his trailer, he watches our preparations, even for sequences involving pyrotechnics and sometimes comes over with ideas.”Chethan also remembered an incident in which another performer was nervous while reacting to Rajinikanth’s strike. As Chethan corrected the performer, Rajinikanth asked him, “Am I doing it right? Is what I’m doing okay?”“That humility, rather than an attitude of knowing everything, is part of his X factor and makes him a genuine collaborator,” Chethan said.Rajinikanth’s X factorChethan added that Rajinikanth’s screen presence and swagger make even simple actions distinctive. Whether he holds a knife or a gun, or simply looks at someone, the actor brings his own style to the moment.He has an unmistakable presence, style and swagger. Give him a knife, a gun or any object — or simply ask him to look — and he brings something distinctive to it. Although we must consider his age, he still comes up with ideas beyond what we have planned or imagined. Sometimes we explain only the sequence, without suggesting a particular gesture, and he surprises us with his interpretation. That is his X factor,” he said.Speaking of ‘Jailer 2’, the film has become the highest-grossing Tamil film of all time surpassing Rajinikanth his 2018 mega hit ‘2.0’. According to trade analyst Sacnilk, the film’s worldwide gross collection has crossed over Rs. 733.35 crore as of Day 12.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sonali Kulkarni on '26 years of Mission Kashmir', praise from the President and more: ‘I have done more than 100 films, but I haven't spoken’- Exclusive
articles.summary: As ‘Mission Kashmir’ completes 26 years, Sonali Kulkarni looks back at playing Neelima Khan in Vidhu Vinod Chopra’s film, her experience of working with
articles.body: As ‘Mission Kashmir’ completes 26 years, Sonali Kulkarni looks back at playing Neelima Khan in Vidhu Vinod Chopra’s film, her experience of working with Sanjay Dutt and Hrithik Roshan, and why the film continues to resonate with audiences. In an exclusive conversation with ETimes, the actor also recalls a memorable interaction with the then President of India, who recognized her for her performance as Ramabai Ambedkar in ‘Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar.' From revisiting films that were ahead of their time to wanting her work to reach a wider audience, Sonali reflects on her journey and the experiences that continue to inspire her.Sonali Kulkarni on completing 26 years of ‘Mission Kashmir’ and why Neelima Khan remains special"‘Mission Kashmir’ has completed 26 years, and I think, as an actor, I have worked on many films that were ahead of their time. ‘Mission Kashmir’ also came at the right time because it was a film made by Vidhu Vinod Chopra himself. Vinod was not only the producer but also the director, which was rare for him.I was really touched by the way he treated all the characters and the way he sketched Neelima Khan, my character. She is a woman who has her sensibilities, spine, and pride intact. She doesn't fear telling her world, her love, and her son that philosophy is one thing and love is another.You need to understand what a nation has sacrificed. You need to understand the facts before you decide that you want to have animosity towards someone.I really liked Neelima Khan's character and the way Vinod treated her. She is Sanjay Dutt's wife and Hrithik's surrogate mother. We talk about women not getting meaty roles, and here is Neelima Khan, standing strong with an immense amount of love, affection, and pride in her heart," she expressed.Sonali Kulkarni on working with Sanjay Dutt: ‘He told me not to take tension'Sonali recalled, "I remember Sanjay being absolutely easy, chilled out, and extremely cooperative on the set. He supported me so well and asked me to relax. He said, ‘Aisa tension leke mat kaam karo.’We had a small scene, which we used to call the bedroom scene. There was nothing like that; it was just a husband and wife, with the wife blushing because they were teasing each other about who said ‘maa’ first and who said ‘papa’ first.It was a very cute scene and filled with affection. But the way the unit started calling it ‘the terrace wala scene’ or ‘the aangan wala scene’ eventually made it our ‘bedroom scene.'I started feeling nervous, and I was given a sleeveless gown. We didn't even have to do anything in the scene. So Sanjay finally told me, ‘Dekh, pehle main nervous rehta hoon aise scenes mein. Uske aage tu bhi nervous rahegi, toh scene kahin nahi jaayega. So, let's relax. It's just a dialogue scene.’He was very sweet."Sonali on witnessing Hrithik Roshan's growing stardom during the shoot"Hrithik, till about 90 percent of the film, had not become the frenzy and heartthrob of India that he later became. But during the last schedule of ‘Mission Kashmir,' I could see the change. There were so many people on the sets just to catch a glimpse of Hrithik, and there used to be security on the set.Hrithik and I got to do the same scene that we had done for our audition, so it was fun," she shared.Sonali opens up on whether ‘Mission Kashmir’ could be made today"Whether ‘Mission Kashmir’ could be made today. It is a unique film because of the time when it was made. Today, we are seeing a lot of films about spies, two nations, and betrayal.But of course, ‘Mission Kashmir’ will always stand apart from the crowd because it is based on strong emotions. If it were made today, I would have still suited the part. We are talking about 26 years ago, and I still had the courage to play Neelima Khan. It goes without saying that I would do anything for Vinod because he's such a sensitive director.It's a lovely thought to imagine having Hrithik, Preity, Sanju, Jackie Sir, and everyone in the film, and we should actually remake the film with Vinod Pradhan's cinematography, Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy's music, and such lovely costumes. We don't have Nitin Desai, though, who was the production designer," she said.On audiences revisiting her films and the beauty of cinema"As I said earlier, yes, I have worked on films that were ahead of their time. People are revisiting ‘Mission Kashmir’. They keep watching ‘Taxi No. 9211.' They keep watching ‘Daayraa’ nowadays. And they keep watching ‘Dr. Ambedkar.'I feel this is the beauty of cinema. You cannot revisit a theater performance in the same way. Though there is an exception, people keep watching ‘Sakharam Binder’ also, which we had shot about 20 years back when Vijay Tendulkar sir was still there with us.But that's the beauty of cinema. My husband and I started watching 'Omkara'. Both of us were talking about certain films, and we somehow missed ‘Omkara’. We can watch it today, and it's such a joy to see the times and the actors, who are ever-evolving. It is so wonderful to see Kareena, Saif, Ajay, and Konkona in that phase of 'Omkara.'In so many of my films, I can see my speech, voice quality, pitch, and body language varying. We have such a rich audience in India. I love reading it when audiences notice the nuances in one's performance,"Biggest misconception about Sonali Kulkarni"The misconception about me has nothing to do with my acting abilities, but many people think that I reside in Pune. I am originally from Pune, and I was the first one among my contemporaries to shift to Mumbai. I remember so many actors from later generations taking the path I took, although they didn't copy me. I shifted to Mumbai much earlier.I never shared a room in a hostel or lived on a cot basis. I have really nice memories of my rented houses. I lived in a chawl in Dadar, then rented a house, and had the smallest studio apartment, which I am very proud of to this day. Then, of course, I bought my own house.As for other misconceptions, I can't really say. I am very happy. I am not publicity-shy, and I have always felt that my work should reach people. Perhaps that is one misconception I would like to fight against in the coming years. I want my work to reach a wider audience because I have done more than 100 films and so much work over the years.Both the volume and quality of my work matter to me. I haven't spoken aloud enough about my own work, but I am coming out of that shyness, which is a welcome phase for me," the actress clarified.On the President of India's recognition for her performance as Ramabai Ambedkar"When we were invited by the President, I remember the security and even what I was wearing. Hrithik and Sanjay were both wearing denims and light blue shirts. The screening was over, and then we had high tea, which was a very magical experience. We were given saucers, then empty cups, then spoons, followed by tea decoction, milk, sugar, and biscuits.You are not exactly awkward, but you are overwhelmed when the President of India is standing close to you and you are having chai with him.Vidhu Vinod Chopra was introducing all of us. He said, ‘This is Sanjay Dutt,’ and went on to introduce him. Then he introduced Hrithik Roshan as the heartthrob of India, with many adjectives.I was standing a little behind when the president looked at me and asked, ‘Are you Rama?’Instinctively, I looked back, thinking there was someone standing behind me. Vinod realized that the president was talking to me and said, ‘No, no, this is Sonali Kulkarni. She played Neelima Khan in the film that you saw just now.’The president said, ‘Of course, I know that.’ He called me closer and asked, ‘Did you play Rama Ambedkar in a film called Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar?’I said, ‘Yes, sir.’ He told me that he had watched my film the previous month and said, ‘What a performance. I loved the film.’He went on talking about me and the film ‘Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar.' I can't tell you how touched I was, how smitten I was.And he didn't stop there. Everybody was speechless. He called his family and close friends and introduced me to everyone. He said, ‘Look who's come. Sonali, who played Ramabai in Dr. Ambedkar. Let's have a photo with you.’That was the epitome of glory or recognition for me, and it remains so to this day. If the first citizen of my country recognizes me so sharply and treats me so fondly, what more could I ask for in life?I should only strive to work better and better, work harder, pour my heart into my work even more, and make our Tricolour feel proud of what I am doing in my career. I have been so driven ever since that day. And that is all, thanks to ‘Mission Kashmir's screening at the President's residence," she concluded with a smile.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Aitana, 27 años y propietaria de tres viviendas: "A mí también se me ha dicho que soy una especuladora por lo que conté en 'La Revuelta"
articles.standfirst: La artista española vendió una de sus propiedades, según revela en GQ
articles.summary: La artista española vendió una de sus propiedades, según revela en GQ
articles.body: El problema de la vivienda sigue preocupando a gran parte de los españoles. La dificultad para acceder a una vivienda en alquiler e, incluso, para adquirir un inmueble no para de aumentar. Aunque es un contratiempo que, especialmente, afecta a las personas de a pie, las estrellas de nuestro país no se quedan al margen. En su última entrevista para GQ, Aitana ha sido muy sincera al respecto. Hay que recordar que la cantante ya tuvo una pequeña polémica tras una aparición en ‘La Revuelta’. Allí dijo tenía cuatro viviendas: una en España, una en Miami y dos en alquiler. De momento, tras el revuelo generado decidió vender una, mientras que la otra la mantiene arrendada, pero “con unas condiciones que no tienen nada que ver con lo que está pasando en el mercado a día de hoy”. A pesar de crear una sociedad inmobiliaria, destaca que es solo para sus propiedades. Sobre sus palabras en ‘La Revuelta’, recuerda que no tenía “conciencia” de lo que era el tema. Además, después se pudo “meter más a fondo” para conocer el problema. A pesar de su posición de “privilegio”, tiene claro que debe usar su altavoz para denunciar la situación. Aitana es contundente tras haber pasado por muchas críticas: “No especulo con la vivienda ni lo voy a querer hacer nunca”. Tampoco rehuye de su obligación fiscal en nuestra nación: “Me compré una casa en Miami para poder trabajar allí, pero tributando siempre en España, porque también dicen que a las personas que ganan más, hay que freírlas a impuestos. Y estoy completamente de acuerdo”. Por último, la artista catalana se pronuncia sobre los grandes tenedores u otras estrellas que acumulan viviendas como inversión. Aunque ella no lo haría, tiene clara la decisión que tomaría al respecto si tuviera la oportunidad: “Tampoco estoy de acuerdo con que una persona tenga 10 casas, pero si las tiene, que se le apliquen todos los impuestos que correspondan”.

articles.summary: He entered to the beats of the dhol, made Korean hearts to the audience and performed in true Punjabi spirit.
articles.body: He entered to the beats of the dhol, made Korean hearts to the audience and performed in true Punjabi spirit. From Gal Ban Gayee to the fan-favourite Oh Ho Ho Ho, the Prince of Bhangra, Sukhbir, got Delhi grooving as he brought Nykaaland, a three-day beauty fest at NSIC grounds to a close on Sunday. “I wasn’t sure if I should say it but I think the girls have more energy here. Girls, you have to show the boys how to do bhangra! That’s your job today,” he said.A special tribute to his fatherAmid whistles and cheers, Sukhbir blew kisses to the audience. Sharing a special anecdote, he said, “Mere pitaji ne puri umar babaji da kaam kitta hai, kirtan kiya hai, jab tak menu yaad hai. Jo bhi shayari likhi, upar wale ke liye likhi. Chhabbis saal pehle maine apne pitaji se request kari ki mere liye ek gaana likhdo aur agla gaana unhone mere liye likha. This (Sauda Khara Khara) is a song that means more to me than others. Thank you very much for coming and making this an amazing time for us.”From childhood faves to the stage “Bahut log kehte hain, ‘I’ve been listening to your songs since I was a child. articles.summary: Actress Srinidhi Shetty became popular with the ‘KGF’ franchise and is gearing up for the release of ‘Aadarsha Kutumbam House No.
articles.body: Actress Srinidhi Shetty became popular with the ‘KGF’ franchise and is gearing up for the release of ‘Aadarsha Kutumbam House No. 47’, starring Venkatesh Daggubati and directed by Trivikram Srinivas. Ahead of its theatrical release, the actress addressed the buzz around her that she demands Rs 7–8 crore as remuneration for a film. She dismissed the reports as rumours.In a conversation with SCREEN, while discussing her upcoming film, Srinidhi Shetty said she has acted in only a few films so far and questioned how she could demand such a large amount.“After the success of the KGF films, they say that I am asking for Rs 7 to Rs 8 crore. I have acted in few films so far. When that is the case, how can I ask for such a huge amount as remuneration? So, it is just a rumour,” she said.Srinidhi Shetty says money is not her prioritySrinidhi Shetty also shared that earning money has never been her only goal. She added that she could have worked in many more films if money had been her main motivation, but she prefers choosing projects based on their stories and characters.“If earning money was my only goal, I could have acted in 30 to 40 films over the last few years. But I do not sign films just for money. I give priority to good stories and quality characters,” she added.The actress has appeared in six films over eight years and admitted that she would like to work more frequently. “I am pretty instinctive with scripts. I want to do more films but they are not coming to me,” she said.Srinidhi Shetty responds to ‘AK47’ and ‘Blast’ comparisonsDuring the interaction, Srinidhi Shetty also addressed comparisons between ‘Aadarsha Kutumbam House No. 47’ and the recently released film ‘Blast’. She said the two films are not similar in their stories, even though both feature family elements and action.“There are no similarities between the two films. Just because both of these films have family elements and action involved, people think they are the same. But that is not true,” she said.She explained that films belonging to the same genre are often compared, but that does not mean their stories are alike. The actress also revealed that ‘AK47’ marks her first attempt at comedy.“This is the first time I have done comedy. I have never done comedy before. So I don’t know how it will come out. It is a good blend of crime, comedy and dark comedy,” she said.Srinidhi Shetty on playing mother in ‘Aadarsha Kutumbam’Srinidhi Shetty also spoke about playing a mother early in her career, saying she had no hesitation about taking on the role. She explained that she does not want to limit herself to one type of character or genre.About ‘Adarsha Kutumbam’Speaking about the film, ‘Adarsha Kutumbam’, Srinidhi Shetty plays Venkatesh’s wife and the female lead. The film also stars Nara Rohith, Nivetha Pethuraj, Yuvina, Raj Prajwal, Rao Ramesh, Satya, Brahmaji, Vennela Kishore and Raghu Babu in key roles.‘Aadarsha Kutumbam House No: 47’ was originally announced for release on October 2 during Gandhi Jayanti but was later shifted to October 9. articles.title: Noah Wyle Is the Sexiest Man Alive! No Second Opinion Needed.
articles.summary: Smoldering intensity, leading-man looks and he loves to do the dishes? No wonder the ‘Pitt’ star has fans swooning — and his wife singing his praises
articles.body:
We all owe Noah Wyle 's wife, Sara , a debt of gratitude. When the Pitt star, 55, first got the news that he was going to be crowned Sexiest Man Alive , he was incredulous. "I thought that sounded like a prank — just not in a million years did I think that this would be an honor bestowed on me," says the actor.

Luckily Sara, 46, was able to convince him that he was, in fact, SMA material. "She thinks I'm a good guy and that the kind of person that I am and the kind of father I am, the kind of husband I am, is worth promoting." he says. "I thought, 'Okay, if you say so.' " Not to mention, "she was very pleased that this reflects well on her taste," he adds.

Read every sexy page of People 's Sexiest Man Alive issue — two days before everyone else, only for People VIPs.

Judging by the way Wyle lit up when she arrived at his shoot at a cliffside Malibu estate this August with their daughter Frances, 11, and their chocolate Lab Lily in tow, it's clear whose opinion matters most. Once on-set, Sara happily cheered him on as he showed off his domestic skills for our social video — whipping up Frances's favorite eggs, cleaning up the kitchen and even folding laundry. And if you needed another reason to swoon, his wife confirms he does all that and more at their Los Angeles home.

For all the prodding needed for Wyle to accept his Sexiest Man Alive status, this isn't his first brush with People 's highest honor. Back in the '90s, when he was stealing hearts as the handsome young Dr. Carter on ER , he and his costars George Clooney , Eriq La Salle and Anthony Edwards graced the cover of the magazine's "Sexy Men of ER " issue. Clooney, of course, went on to claim the Sexiest Man Alive crown twice. But Wyle? Somehow we let him get away.

Now with The Pitt , his latest zeitgeisty medical drama ( which returns for season 3 in January on HBO Max), delivering what Wyle calls the "second lightning strike in my life" (and two consecutive best actor Emmys), it's about time to give Dr. Robby his due.

Here Wyle sits down with People' s editor in chief Charlotte Triggs for a revealing conversation about fame, family and finally getting the cover he deserves.

Congrats on being our new Sexiest Man Alive. What did your kids [Owen, 24, Auden, 21, and Frances] think when you told them?

My son is super practical. He was like, "Oh, this is going to make my life so much harder now. But that's cool, Dad. But also, you invite a lot of haters too." My older daughter was just like, "No way, no way." Because I think she's going to tease me about this for the next 50 years.

Do you think anything will be different?

I hope this changes everything. I hope it's just wine and roses, milk and honey from here on out. [ Laughs ] No, I don't, but I am going to take a lot of ribbing from friends and family for sure.

" I'M A GEMINI — I'M A BIT MERCURIAL. I TEND TO DO THINGS INTENSELY FOR FINITE PERIODS OF TIME "

I think he'll be amused and feel, hopefully, like a proud papa, that I've come of gray-haired age.

In middle school I went from sort of string bean-y to short and stocky, then stretched out again in high school. But that short, stocky period was rife with insecurity.

I wasn't a very good athlete, and I wasn't a great student. So I just kept looking for my tribe, and I found them in the theater department.

When did you finally feel comfortable in your own skin?

I was so hoping today was going to be the day. "Look at you. You're the Sexiest Man Alive. Finally you can be comfortable in your own skin." Not yet. I like being in other people's skin. I like putting on characters. I get self-conscious. It's still the hardest kind of interaction for me, speaking without a script as myself.

I've heard other actors describe that experience.

You get into this because you are a natural observer. Then that privacy is immediately taken from you if you get any notoriety. It could be a hard thing to reconcile. It took me a long time. The Pitt gives me the opportunity to do it differently than I did the first time — with a little bit more presence and a little bit more composure.

How were you at dealing with fame the first time around with ER ?

Faking it really well. Those were heady times. There was a complete 180 that happened almost overnight after my 22nd birthday. When I came out the other end of the ER experience, I was 37, married [to ex Tracy Warbin] with two kids in a totally different situation. But all of that felt like it had gone by in a blur.

What's been one of your most memorable fan encounters?

The other night I was sitting in this restaurant with my wife and another couple, and this older couple came to the table, and they said, "We love The Pitt . We haven't missed an episode. I just had surgery. Would you mind taking a look?" And she rolled up her pant leg and showed me the freshest stitches I've seen in a long time. And I said, "It looks like it's healing nicely. Are you putting full weight on it?" My wife's like, "Are you doing this right now?"

So people think you're an actual doctor?

Oh, absolutely. And occasionally I do too.

Oh yeah, tons. I work with a guy named Dr. Joe Sachs, who is about to receive a lifetime achievement award from Stanford Medical. Also through the company FIGS [where Wyle is a global brand ambassador ], I've found very inspirational, really impressive people who are currently in the workforce. I find them incredibly noble.

What's a typical day like when you're not working?

I usually make breakfast for my wife and my daughter. I have a daily journal practice. I try to exercise a little bit every day. I do Pilates or kettle-bells, and I take my dogs for a walk. I try to read a little bit every day. Try not to scroll too much on my phone. But I rarely get a day off.

I am the dish maven. The sink is my domain. And I would recommend more guys get into the dishwashing, because it's very therapeutic.

The ones I'm least proud of at the moment are my Instagram shopping habits. A lot of survival gear. Those guys always get me. "You think you're prepared? You're not. You know what you need? You need this bucket of s---."

I don't like to be late. I would rather get there 5 to 10 minutes early, find a good place to park, not feel stressed and have a drink at the bar.

What's your favorite place in the world?

I'm kind of a homebody. I have a place up in Santa Ynez, California, that's my go-to sanctuary.

It sounds odd, but I have a talent for catching flies live. Catch and release. I have really very, very fast hands.

What's the most romantic thing you've done?

When my wife and I were first courting, I had two kids from a previous marriage, and we weren't always able to be together because I'd have them, and for almost a year I didn't introduce everybody. So when we weren't together, I would make these gifts for my wife. I'd make a book with photographs and mementos of things that we'd done on dates and drawings and poems and things that I'd find. Just ways of being able to do something for her when we were apart that I thought she'd like when we saw each other again.

We've been trying to do them with more regularity. My daughter went away to sleepaway camp for two weeks, and after we got through the first 48 hours of like, "I don't know what we do without a child to give all of our love and attention to," we were like, "Oh wait, I think we used to give it to each other." And then we had a great time. A great date could be staying in. It could be going out. It could be going someplace to stay in. But usually it involves eating.

Once we were driving a car full of children to breakfast. I love hawks — that's one of my favorite animals — and I saw this hawk soaring, and I was just about to say, "Hey, everybody, look at this beautiful hawk!" And I realized it was soaring right into my car. There was no avoiding it. I hit it, and I saw in the rearview mirror that the car behind me hit it, and I let out a sound that was somewhere between a scream and a cry. My wife immediately knows that this is going to ruin my week, and she says the only three words that would have kept me from wanting to turn the car off the road. She said, "He chose you." She always knows the words to defuse the bomb.

At a party, I like to ... Check out the books on the shelf in the library. Or pet the dog. I have an irrational fear of ... Maggots. It's more of a revulsion. I dream about ... Flying. Falling. Having my teeth fall out. Being late. Being lost. All sorts of odd dreams. Mr first nickname was ... Wyle Coyote. My first car was ... A 1988 sky blue Dodge Shadow. Not a very sexy car. I used to leave it perpetually unlocked, and homeless people would sleep in the back and pee in it. The movie that always makes me cry is ... The Champ . Ricky Schroder crying over Jon Voight's dead body broke me up. Left on my bucket list is ... Hosting SNL. The title of my memoir would be ... Noah's Arc .

That was the most life-changing event in my life. They handed my son to me, and I was like, "Now I get it. It's not about me, it's about you." That's when I quit ER . He was born on, like, a Tuesday. I went to work on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, spent time with him for the first time on Saturday, went back to work the following Monday and was looking at my watch, going, "Come on, what are we doing?" I'd never tried to rush through work to get home, and I thought, "Well, where do you want to be?" So I tendered my resignation. I called it a divorce with visitation rights and came back for the finale.

I've got a wonderful wife. I've got wonderful kids. I've got four parents that are still alive and able to, you know, feed themselves and have dinner and give advice. I'm grateful for my work. I'm grateful for my colleagues. I'm grateful for friends and mentors—and the teachers that I've had.

articles.title: Harry Kane y el Rolex Daytona de 1,2 millones de euros que lució en la gala del Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: Harry Kane lució en la gala del Balón de Oro 2026 un exclusivo Rolex Cosmograph Daytona de oro blanco con zafiros azules
articles.summary: Harry Kane lució en la gala del Balón de Oro 2026 un exclusivo Rolex Cosmograph Daytona de oro blanco con zafiros azules
articles.body: Harry Kane se convirtió este lunes, 26 de octubre, en el gran protagonista de la gala del Balón de Oro 2026. El delantero del Bayern de Múnich recibió el galardón individual más prestigioso del fútbol por primera vez en su carrera y puso fin a 25 años de espera para Inglaterra, que no celebraba la victoria de uno de sus futbolistas desde Michael Owen en 2001. Sin embargo, además de su histórico triunfo deportivo, hubo otro detalle que llamó la atención de los amantes del lujo: el espectacular reloj que llevaba en la muñeca. El futbolista inglés acudió a la ceremonia celebrada en el London Palladium con un Rolex Cosmograph Daytona Blue Sapphire, una pieza de oro blanco de 18 quilates cuyo valor en el mercado puede rondar los 1,2 millones de euros. Se trata de una de las versiones más exclusivas de la conocida colección de la firma suiza, con una combinación de materiales preciosos y piedras preciosas que la convierte en un objeto especialmente codiciado por los coleccionistas. El modelo que lució Harry Kane destaca por su caja de 40 milímetros fabricada en oro blanco de 18 quilates. Su elemento más llamativo es el bisel, engastado con 36 zafiros azules de talla baguette que sustituyen a la tradicional escala taquimétrica del Daytona. El resultado es una pieza que conserva la identidad deportiva del cronógrafo, pero la lleva al terreno de la alta joyería. La esfera también contribuye a su singularidad. Está elaborada con obsidiana de tonalidad plateada, una piedra natural que aporta profundidad y matices al conjunto. Los índices con piedras preciosas y los contadores del cronógrafo completan un diseño que combina la estética característica de Rolex con una ejecución mucho más exclusiva que la de las versiones habituales de la colección. El reloj pertenece a las referencias que Rolex no comercializa de forma ordinaria en su catálogo, conocidas en el sector como off-catalogue. Estas piezas pueden tener una disponibilidad extremadamente limitada y suelen despertar un interés especial entre los coleccionistas. Su acceso no funciona como el de un modelo convencional que cualquier cliente puede encargar en un distribuidor. El Cosmograph Daytona, presentado originalmente en 1963, nació como un instrumento para pilotos y aficionados al automovilismo. Con el paso de las décadas, se ha convertido en uno de los cronógrafos más reconocibles de la relojería de lujo. Las versiones con piedras preciosas han ampliado su atractivo entre quienes buscan ejemplares excepcionales, alejados de las configuraciones más habituales. La elección del reloj acompañó una de las noches más importantes de la carrera del delantero inglés. Kane se impuso a Kylian Mbappé y Lamine Yamal en la votación del Balón de Oro masculino, después de una temporada 2025-2026 en la que sus cifras goleadoras y los títulos conquistados con el Bayern de Múnich reforzaron su candidatura. El inglés se convirtió así en el primer futbolista de su país en ganar el premio desde Michael Owen, que lo consiguió hace un cuarto de siglo. Además, durante la misma ceremonia recibió el reconocimiento al Delantero del Año, conocido también como premio Gerd Müller.

articles.title: Imran Khan gets temporary relief, as 'leave India' notice put on hold, court to hear the actor's plea on November 2
articles.summary: Actor Imran Khan has received temporary relief in his legal battle against a notice asking him to leave India by October 28.
articles.body: Actor Imran Khan has received temporary relief in his legal battle against a notice asking him to leave India by October 28. The Bombay High Court on Tuesday adjourned the hearing on his petition to November 2 at 3 pm after the Centre sought additional time to respond. The development comes just a day before the deadline issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO). Imran, a US citizen who holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, has challenged the directive, questioning its legal basis and calling it arbitrary.According to Bar and Bench, a division bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna heard the matter briefly on Tuesday. Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh, appearing for the Centre, requested that the hearing be postponed until November 2. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, who was expected to join the proceedings through video conference, could not attend.Senior advocate Venkatesh Dhond, representing Imran, brought the urgency of the matter to the court's attention, pointing out that the actor was required to leave India the following day under the FRRO directive. "Lordship may keep it on Monday," the ASG told the bench. "But I have to leave tomorrow (according to the FRRO directive)," he responded.The Centre's counsel subsequently assured the court that no immediate action would be taken against Imran before the next hearing, clarifying that the assurance was being given orally. The court then deferred the matter to November 2 at 3 pm, directing that the order challenged by the actor remain in abeyance until the next hearing.The legal dispute follows an incident on October 10, when Mumbai Police detained Imran near August Kranti Maidan. The actor was reportedly present at the location during a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. His partner, Lekha Washington, and cousin Zayn Marie Khan were also detained.Four days later, on October 14, the FRRO issued a Leave India Notice (LIN), directing Imran to leave the country by October 28. The notice invoked Sections 7(2)(C) and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.Challenging the directive, Imran filed a writ petition titled Imran Khan Pal v. Union of India & Ors. through lawyers Zulfiquar Memon, Parvez Memon and Kunal Vajani. He described the notice as “arbitrary, illegal, perverse and drastic” and questioned the grounds on which it had been issued, alleging that it came “without disclosing any reasons, supporting material, or specific statutory contravention.”The petition argued that the authorities had issued the notice without conducting an inquiry, serving a show-cause notice or giving him an opportunity to present his side. It also alleged that the action was based on a politically motivated complaint and reflected “patent non-application of mind.”Imran further denied actively participating in the protest, maintaining that no demonstration was underway when he reached the spot. He also questioned the justification for his detention alongside his family members. Contesting the proportionality of the FRRO's action, the petition stated: “Not only is the notice manifestly disproportionate, if implemented, it would reduce the very principles of natural justice that the Respondents are duty bound to uphold to nothing but a dead letter.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
